analyst_view.overall: CSKA Sofia (28th, 1 pt) host Trabzonspor (12th, 6 pts) in the first European night at the rebuilt Balgarska Armia; a win would put CSKA back in the race for the top 24, while Trabzonspor's Thomas Reis wants two wins from the last three games to chase the top eight after the home defeat to Freiburg. CSKA have no new injuries; Teodor Ivanov is recovering from a knock and Markus Gisdol did not rule him out, while Kotar is unavailable. Trabzonspor travelled with 20 players and left eight at home for treatment: Dju (their top European scorer), Folcarelli, Batagov, Simsir and Yokuslu, plus Savic, Muci and, new since the last view, playmaker Ruslan Malinovskyi; the numbers only count Simsir and Yokuslu. Trabzonspor fans are banned from the away end, and CSKA added about 2,000 seats for home supporters; an afternoon team-news page again lists Malinovskyi (knee), Yokuslu, Simsir, Batagov, Folcarelli and Dju as out. French referee Jeremie Pignard is confirmed, and the numbers already add about 13% to cards for his record.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, 1.6 of them Trabzonspor's, and they only take off Simsir and Yokuslu. Two Turkish and Bulgarian reports now confirm Malinovskyi also stayed at home, so Trabzonspor are without Dju, Folcarelli, Muci and Malinovskyi, most of their creativity behind Onuachu and Salah; Savic's absence weakens their defence against a CSKA side that must attack, which keeps the size small. I move from -2% to -3%, about 2.6 goals.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners, split evenly, already nudged up for CSKA's recent corner count. CSKA must push at home in front of a bigger crowd and Trabzonspor use their full-backs, but the absentees are mostly central players and don't change how either side plays wide, so I stay at about 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.8 cards, well above a usual game, because they add 13% for referee Pignard's record on top of both sides' recent bookings. A loud, near-full home stadium can heat things up, but with no away fans allowed and the figure already high, nothing specific points further, so I stay at about 5.8.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.4 shots, already lifted 12% for CSKA's recent volume. CSKA chasing a first league-phase win against a Trabzonspor defence without Savic should keep the game open, while a Trabzonspor side without Dju, Muci and Malinovskyi may shoot less; the two roughly cancel, so I stay at about 29.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.2 shots on target, already raised for CSKA's recent accuracy. Without Dju, Folcarelli, Muci and now Malinovskyi, a regular source of long-range efforts, Trabzonspor lose much of their finishing and chance creation, which the numbers don't know; Savic's absence may let CSKA in a bit more, so I lean only a little lower: -3% gives about 9.9.
